edges.note: A single choke point wrapping malloc/free is the tactic's 'explicit resource manager' at allocator granularity, mediating all access to the memory resource.

edges.cite: Gregory, Game Engine Architecture: the resource management layer of the canonical engine layering performs asynchronous asset streaming
edges.note: The engine layering's resource-management layer depends on background streaming as its load-bearing mechanism.
Streaming acquires only the assets needed for the player's current locality, progressively - a domain specialization of partial acquisition.
Header/footer tags remove the search work otherwise needed to find free neighbors, making coalescing on free constant-time.
Boundary tags are an internal mechanism of general variable-size heap allocators.
Power-of-two splitting/coalescing bounds external fragmentation and keeps free-block management cheap - efficiency of the memory resource itself.
Competing constant/log-bounded dynamic allocator designs for kernels and embedded heaps.

edges.cite: Nygard, Release It! (Bulkheads): the same partitioning principle applies from thread pools and connection pools up to servers and clusters
edges.note: Same-name-two-realms pair: in-process resource compartments realize the deployment-scale isolation pattern.
Cells are bulkhead compartments at whole-deployment scale; the compartmentalization mechanism is what makes a cell an isolation unit.
Hides result-size and allocation knowledge behind the function interface; the caller depends only on the returned handle plus paired deallocator.
No hidden dynamic allocation in the callee: the caller controls placement (stack/static), removing allocation-failure and leak fault classes from the callee.

edges.cite: Preschern, Fluent C (memory/data-return patterns): Caller-Owned Buffer and Callee Allocates presented as alternative solutions to returning data across an API
edges.note: Opposite ownership placements for the same buffer-passing problem.
Less-vital components sacrificing their memory so critical tasks keep running is graceful degradation applied to the memory resource (Weir & Noble, Small Memory Software).
Recovers memory lost to fragmentation, raising effective utilization of a fixed memory budget.
POSA2 Component Configurator binds component implementations at runtime via link/unlink - the runtime end of the defer-binding spectrum.
Runtime relinking of implementations without recompiling or restarting is the mechanism behind in-service code upgrade.
Defers or avoids physical copies until mutation, sharing one instance among readers.
Cheap COW snapshots are a standard mechanism for capturing the known-good state the rollback tactic reverts to (filesystems, databases, fork-based checkpoints).
The memory-sourcing policy is a client-chosen parameter rather than hard-coded - binding the allocation decision late.
Keeps only the current working portion in RAM, processing from secondary storage - stretches a fixed memory budget (Small Memory Software).
Exactly-one-owner discipline with explicit transfer prevents the leak/double-free/dangling fault class before it arises.
Deterministic release of unmanaged resources prevents handle/connection exhaustion faults in garbage-collected runtimes.
POSA3: acquiring resources at startup moves unpredictable acquisition latency out of the time-critical path, bounding runtime response.
Eagerly acquired resources are typically held and handed out via a pool (POSA3 relates the two patterns).
Safe deferred reclamation is load-bearing for lock-free concurrent data structures; without it concurrent readers cannot run against concurrent removal.

edges.cite: Hart, McKenney, Brown, Walpole (2007), 'Performance of memory reclamation for lockless synchronization' - directly compares epoch-based reclamation and hazard pointers as alternative schemes
edges.note: Competing deferred-reclamation schemes for lock-free structures.
The tactic's caching form depends on an eviction policy (LRU/LFU/priority) to bound the copy store; POSA3 Evictor is that component.
An evictor commonly manages which pooled resources are released or swapped out under pressure.
Guaranteeing the paired release action around client code prevents leak and unbalanced-acquire faults even on early exit.
Block/lambda-based paired-action guarantee in languages without deterministic destructors; same guarantee, different vehicle.
Worst-case fixed sizes make every freed block exactly reusable, eliminating fragmentation-induced allocation failure.
Push/pop on a list threaded through the free blocks themselves gives O(1) allocate/free with zero per-block metadata allocation.
Fixed-block pools are conventionally implemented as free lists threaded through the unused blocks.
Automatic reclamation removes the dangling-pointer, double-free, and most leak fault classes from the program.
Managed abstract-machine runtimes (JVM, CLR, interpreter VMs) depend on GC as the memory-management substrate of their instruction-set abstraction.
A runtime mechanism internal to concurrent/moving collectors.
Read barriers are what make fully concurrent compacting collectors (low, bounded pause times) possible - the mechanism behind pause-time-bounded GC.
A compiler/runtime mechanism internal to generational and incremental collectors.
Write barriers enable generational/incremental collection, keeping individual collection pauses small and bounded instead of whole-heap stop-the-world.
Per-thread published hazards make lock-free reads safe against concurrent reclamation (Michael 2004) - load-bearing for parallel access to shared structures.
Indirection slots in writable storage let ROM-resident data/behavior be rebound after the fact - late binding applied to read-only memory (Small Memory Software).
Hooks give the illusion of writable ROM: the two patterns are paired in Small Memory Software's read-only memory chapter.
Skips teardown bookkeeping for whole-program-lifetime allocations, delegating reclamation to OS process teardown.

edges.cite: Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications ch. 8: the leader holds a lease that must be renewed; expiry lets another node take over
edges.note: Time-bounded, auto-expiring grants are the standard mechanism for holding and safely relinquishing the leader role.
Bounds render cost and live UI-node count to the viewport instead of the full data set.
Materializes only the visible part of the list plus a small margin - partial acquisition applied to UI nodes.
POSA3 Lookup - providers register, users query a lookup service - is the pattern-level realization of Bass's discover tactic (matching requests to providers via a discovery service).
A lookup/registration service performs the distributor connector's naming and registration duty in the Taylor-Medvidovic connector taxonomy.
Pointer-bump allocation plus wholesale reset removes per-object allocation and free bookkeeping entirely.
The arena/bump allocator is the concrete mechanism realizing Small Memory Software's Memory Discard discipline (allocate from a workspace, discard wholesale).
Bulk reclamation of a whole temporary workspace eliminates per-object deallocation work.
Per-component memory budgets with failing over-budget allocations are the space half of enforced partitioning.
Loading each phase into a shared memory region from secondary storage is the mechanism by which one-resident-program-at-a-time structures fit the memory budget.
A manager separate from clients and managed objects, controlling creation/access/destruction, is exactly the tactic's interposed explicit resource manager.
Hard time/space-partitioned real-time systems (ARINC 653 class) prohibit or severely restrict demand paging because it destroys temporal determinism.
Acquiring only the part of a large resource needed now keeps peak resource usage proportional to actual demand (POSA3).
Fixed-size block checkout/return is O(1) with no fragmentation, giving the deterministic allocation times hard real-time budgets require.
RTOS kernels and applications rely on fixed-block pools (message blocks, queue buffers) because task-time heap allocation is non-deterministic.
Pooling narrowed to fixed-size memory blocks with per-type/per-size pools.
Recycling released resources amortizes acquisition/release cost across many uses (POSA3 Pooling's stated motivation).
The preforked/prethreaded server structure is a startup-time pool of processes/threads; the pooling mechanism is its substrate.
Tying release to deterministic object destruction prevents leak and unreleased-resource faults on every exit path, including exceptions.
Mission calibration: RAII is the C++/Rust realization of the deterministic dispose/scoped-finalization discipline, with the compiler inserting the dispose call.
Placing immutable code/data in ROM/flash reserves the scarcer writable RAM for mutable state (Small Memory Software).
Automatic reclamation when the last reference drops prevents dangling-pointer and leak faults without a tracing collector.

edges.cite: Jones, Hosking, Moss, The Garbage Collection Handbook: reference counting and tracing presented as the two fundamental families of automatic reclamation
edges.note: Direct (counting) vs indirect (tracing) reclamation; trade determinism against cycle handling and mutator overhead.

edges.cite: Bass-Clements-Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice, Defer Binding tactic: names resource/configuration files as a deployment/startup-time binding mechanism
edges.note: Configuration and read-only resources in external files bind values at startup instead of compile time.
POSA3's dedicated lifecycle manager is the tactic's 'interpose an explicit resource manager' stated as a full pattern.
Defining the complete special-member set prevents double-free/shallow-copy resource faults from compiler-generated members.
The rule is what makes RAII owner types copy/move-correct; zero means delegating ownership to existing RAII members.
Guaranteed cleanup/rollback on scope exit prevents leaked resources and half-done state on early returns and exceptions.
By its own definition an ad-hoc RAII object for an arbitrary cleanup action.
One stored copy referenced from many places instead of duplication (Small Memory Software; interning, flyweight-style structure sharing).
Caching freed objects in constructed state (Bonwick, USENIX 1994) removes per-allocation initialization/teardown work from the hot path.
Per-type fixed-size pools refined with constructed-state caching and cache-coloring.
The embedded inline buffer removes a heap allocation (and its indirection) from the common small case.

edges.cite: Bass-Clements-Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice 3rd ed., availability tactics: Exception Prevention lists 'abstract data types, such as smart pointers' as an implementing mechanism
edges.note: Bass names smart pointers directly as an exception-prevention mechanism.
unique_ptr/shared_ptr are the canonical RAII owner types for dynamically allocated objects.
Automatic storage cannot leak, dangle past scope-checked lifetimes, or fragment - defaulting to it removes heap fault classes.

edges.cite: ARINC 653: partition memory and resources are statically configured in build-time configuration tables; mission calibration example (ARINC-653 partitioning constrains static allocation policy)
edges.note: Partitioned avionics architectures mandate static allocation inside partitions.
No runtime allocation means the allocation-failure and fragmentation fault classes cannot arise - the rationale behind MISRA-C/DO-178 bans on dynamic memory.
The two opposed memory strategies of Small Memory Software's allocation chapter: fixed worst-case at startup vs on-demand heap.
Pairing every accumulation with a purging mechanism (Nygard) prevents resource-exhaustion failures from arising, rather than detecting them.

edges.cite: Masmano, Ripoll, Crespo, Real, 'TLSF: a New Dynamic Memory Allocator for Real-Time Systems' (ECRTS 2004): O(1) worst-case allocation/free motivated by real-time bounded-response requirements
edges.note: The allocator exists precisely to bound worst-case allocation time for real-time systems.
TLSF's two-level bitmap indexes an array of segregated free lists.
Sizing memory to actual demand instead of static worst case raises utilization of a fixed budget (Small Memory Software).
Partitioned hard real-time systems ban or bound on-demand heap allocation inside partitions for determinism.
Non-owning references break reference-count cycles and prevent lapsed-listener leaks - removing leak faults by construction.
weak refs are the standard cycle-breaking complement to counted strong references (weak_ptr beside shared_ptr).

notes: All 56 g11 (resource-management) elements bridged; unbridged list empty. 65 cross-realm edges (realizes/enables/constrains incl. 3 constrains from time-and-space-partitioning), 24 within-realm/implements extras, 10 sourced. The group is memory/resource management, where the arch catalog is thin: many elements land on the (specific but heavily shared) Bass tactics exception-prevention, reduce-computational-overhead, and increase-resource-usage-efficiency. MISSING arch targets that would sharpen these bridges: (1) virtual memory / memory hierarchy as an architecture element (paging, memory-overlay, data-files currently anchor via constrains or generic efficiency tactics); (2) a managed-runtime / garbage-collected-runtime architecture construct (GC family currently anchors to virtual-machine-architectural-style + tactics); (3) a checkpoint/snapshot architecture element (copy-on-write anchors to rollback-tactic prose mention of snapshots); (4) a memory-budgeting/footprint tactic at system level (Small Memory Software's system-scale Memory Limit strategy) for memory-limit, captain-oates, read-only-memory; (5) a resource-reservation/admission-control-for-memory tactic for eager-acquisition and static-allocation beyond bound-execution-times.
